HDOC Day-25 Activity
Question: Write a menu-driven C program using switch-case to display four decreasing patterns using
nested loops without arrays. Each pattern is implemented in a separate parameterless void function. Prepare
the algorithm and test cases, compile, execute, and verify the results.
Step 1: Understanding the Problem
Input: Menu choice (1-5), number of rows n (for options 1-4). Output: The chosen decreasing pattern, an
error message for an invalid choice, or Exit. The program accepts row counts 1-20 to keep output
manageable.
Step 2: Standard Test Case Table
Test Input Expected output Actual output Result
1 Choice 1, n=4 Stars in rows 4,3,2,1 Matches Pass
2 Choice 2, n=4 1..4, 1..3, 1..2, 1 Matches Pass
3 Choice 3, n=4 4444, 333, 22, 1 Matches Pass
4 Choice 4, n=4 4321, 321, 21, 1 Matches Pass
5 Choice 1, n=1 One star Matches Pass
6 Choice 2, n=0 then 2 Error; then rows 1 2 / 1 Matches Pass
7 Choice 9 Invalid menu choice Matches Pass
8 Choice 5 Goodbye! Matches Pass
Step 3: Algorithm and Evaluation
1. Start.
2. Display menu: 1 Stars; 2 Natural numbers; 3 Repeated numbers; 4 Reverse numbers; 5 Exit.
3. Read choice and use switch(choice).
4. For options 1-4, call the corresponding parameterless void function.
5. In the chosen function, read n and repeat input until 1 <= n <= 20.
6. Use an outer loop i from n down to 1.
7. Use a nested inner loop: print i stars (option 1); 1 to i (option 2); i repeated i times (option 3); or i down to 1
(option 4).
8. Print a newline after every row.
9. For an invalid menu choice, display an error. For option 5, exit. Otherwise redisplay menu.
10. Stop.
Evaluation: The nested loop runs one fewer iteration per row. All four patterns match the examples for n=4.
Input validation prevents non-positive or excessive row counts; invalid menu selections return to the menu.
Step 4: Complete C Program
#include <stdio.h>
int read_rows(void) {
int n;
do {
printf("Enter number of rows (1-20): ");
if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1) return 0;
if (n < 1 || n > 20) printf("Invalid rows. Enter 1 to 20.\n");
} while (n < 1 || n > 20);
return n;
}
void stars(void) {
int n=read_rows();
for(int i=n;i>=1;i--) {
for(int j=1;j<=i;j++) printf("* ");
printf("\n");
}
}
void natural(void) {
int n=read_rows();
for(int i=n;i>=1;i--) {
for(int j=1;j<=i;j++) printf("%d ",j);
printf("\n");
}
}
void repeated(void) {
int n=read_rows();
for(int i=n;i>=1;i--) {
for(int j=1;j<=i;j++) printf("%d ",i);
printf("\n");
}
}
void reverse(void) {
int n=read_rows();
for(int i=n;i>=1;i--) {
for(int j=i;j>=1;j--) printf("%d ",j);
printf("\n");
}
}
int main(void) {
int choice;
do {
printf("\n1. Decreasing right-angled triangle\n2. Decreasing natural-number pattern\n3. Decreasing repeated-number
if(scanf("%d", &choice)!=1) { printf("Invalid input.\n"); return 1; }
switch(choice) {
case 1: stars(); break;
case 2: natural(); break;
case 3: repeated(); break;
case 4: reverse(); break;
case 5: printf("Goodbye!\n"); break;
default: printf("Invalid menu choice.\n");
}
} while(choice!=5);
return 0;
}
Step 4: Complete C Program (continued)
